I can solve this, but the picture’s wiring is ambiguous at a couple of diagonal/bridge resistors (I can’t confidently tell which nodes R4 and the left/down diagonal connect to). Can you either

• upload a higher-resolution crop of the network, or  
• confirm this node mapping (quick yes/no):

Nodes (left→right, top/bottom)
- A —R1(6Ω)— N1  
- N1 —R2(8Ω)— B (vertical)  
- N1 —R3(4Ω)— N2 (top center)  
- N1 —R4(8Ω)— N3 (bottom middle)  ← **is this correct?**  
- N3 —R5(4Ω)— B  
- N2 —R6(6Ω)— N3 (vertical)  
- N3 —R7(8Ω)— N4 (bottom right)  
- N2 —R8(10Ω)— N5 (top right)  
- N2 —R9(6Ω)— N4 (diagonal)  
- N5 —R10(2Ω)— N4

If that mapping is correct I’ll compute Req between A and B and show the full reduction/solver steps. If not, paste a clearer crop or tell me which node R4 actually connects to.

Got it — with the node mapping you confirmed, I solved the network by nodal analysis (apply 1 V at A, B = 0). Results:

Node voltages (relative to B):
- N1 = 0.400000 V  
- N2 = 0.300000 V  
- N3 = 0.200000 V  
- N4 = 0.266667 V  
- N5 = 0.272222 V  

Total current drawn from A = 0.100000 A, so the equivalent resistance between A and B is:

# Req = 1 V / 0.1 A = 10.0 Ω

If you want the step-by-step algebraic reduction (showing matrix, equation system, or a Δ–Y transform path), I’ll write it out.
